description: A new pressure-test scenario that hunts the break the shared federation pattern (chief/51 ADR, chief/52 §-edits) must survive: two authorities in one fabric, cross-authority same_as reconciliation plus registry peering plus per-project CAS replication on reference (ROADMAP.md Phase F1). koine promotes a spec only after a concrete pressure test fails to break it (CLAUDE.md conventions), so this scenario is the gate that lets the three federation §-edits re-ratify. Follows the existing scenarios/ convention (replayable, cross-plane assertions) as in scenarios/e2e-worlds-to-fabric.md and scenarios/e2e-media-transform.md. PARKED: gated on chief/51 + chief/52 and on a real >1-authority deployment target (ROADMAP.md: nothing built until a deployment needs more than one authority). Public-safe: bind roles, illustrative CURIEs use the KINP §3.4 placeholder namespaces.
verify: python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('schemas/*.json')]; print('schemas ok')"

userStories.title: A two-authority pressure scenario hunting the shared-pattern break
userStories.description: Author a scenarios/ pressure test with two identity authorities in one fabric, driving cross-authority same_as reconciliation, registry peering, and per-project CAS replication on reference — written to find a break, not to assert correctness (CLAUDE.md conventions).
acceptanceCriteria: A new scenarios/ file (e.g. scenarios/e2e-multi-authority.md) defines a replayable pressure test with TWO authorities and exercises all three federation surfaces the ADR unified: cross-authority same_as reconciliation (KINP), peering discovery registries (KCB), and per-project CAS replicating on reference (KMI).

The scenario asserts the invariants the federation pattern must preserve — offline-first minting still works, content-addressed identity stays byte-stable across authorities/stores, and no query-time merge produces a false cross-authority identity — and is written adversarially (prefer finding a break).

It follows the scenarios/ convention (cross-plane assertion vocabulary, replayable steps) and, per scenarios/README.md, illustrative CURIEs use the KINP §3.4 placeholder namespaces; it names no deployment or product.

userStories.title: Record the re-ratification resolution across the three specs
userStories.description: Wire the scenario back to the three federation §-edits so a clean pass re-ratifies them, matching how existing re-validations record a Resolution note.
acceptanceCriteria: The scenario carries a Resolution / note recording which KINP/KCB/KMI spec versions its pass gates, mirroring the 'Re-validation' sections in the existing scenarios.
On a clean pass the three federation §-edits (chief/52) may return from candidate to ratified; the scenario states this explicitly and each affected spec's changelog can cite it.
schemas/*.json still parse; no schema twin changes are required by this scenario (it is a control/data-plane behavior test, not a shape change).
